title: Why Do You Get a STITCH When You Run? 🏃
description:
That stab under your ribs when you run is not a muscle cramp: when scientists wired up runners mid-stitch, the muscles were calm. The best guess today is friction. Your belly has a slippery two-layer lining, one layer on the wall and one around your organs; running bounces the organs, a full stomach presses the layers together, and the outer layer is the one that feels sharp, pinpoint pain. Nobody has proven it yet. It is probably not your breathing muscle either: people get stitches riding horses and camels. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

What tends to help: slow down, bend forward, and go easy on big meals and sugary drinks before a run. Next up: what really happens when you crack your knuckles.
